Users across an entire building suddenly lose all connectivity, link lights flash rapidly, and switch CPUs spike. The event began after someone connected a small desktop switch. What is happening?
A Layer 2 loop is causing a broadcast storm
After a core switch replacement, traffic between buildings takes a slower path than before. Which cause fits best?
The replacement became an unintended STP root, changing path selection
The DHCP lease time is too short
An employee relocates to a new desk and finds they are now on the guest subnet instead of corporate. Which single change explains this?
The new switch port is assigned to the wrong VLAN
A branch with a single uplink to headquarters can reach HQ servers but nothing on the internet, and the router shows no 0.0.0.0/0 entry. What is missing?
Several new laptops at a busy conference receive 169.254 addresses while earlier arrivals got valid leases. What is the most probable cause?
The DHCP scope ran out of available addresses
A workstation reaches other hosts on its own subnet but cannot reach anything beyond it. Its configured gateway address is on a completely different subnet. What should be corrected?
A server and a desktop both intermittently drop off the network, and an administrator notices one IP appearing on two MAC addresses. What is the issue?
A host configured with mask 255.255.0.0 on a network designed as /24 can reach some stations but behaves oddly toward others. What is wrong?
The subnet mask does not match the network design
A firewall change intended to permit a new application instead blocks it entirely, while all other traffic is fine. What is the likely cause?
The ACL lacks a permit rule for the application or has the rules in the wrong order
Phones in VLAN 40 cannot register, and a packet capture shows they never receive an IP, while VLAN 40's DHCP server is reachable from other VLANs. What should be checked first?
Whether the VLAN 40 gateway has an ip helper-address pointing to the DHCP server
A technician adds a redundant switch uplink for resilience and the network continues working with no apparent change. Why is there no loop?
STP placed one of the redundant links in a blocking state
Workstations in one department can reach the internet but cannot reach a specific internal subnet, while the internet and other internal subnets work. What routing cause fits?
The router is missing a specific route to that internal subnet
A static-IP printer stops responding each time a particular laptop powers on. What is the root cause?
The printer and laptop are configured with the same IP address
Hosts on a /25 subnet cannot reach hosts whose addresses fall in the other half of the original /24 range, even though they share a switch. Why?
The /25 mask splits the range into two separate subnets that require routing between them
A new VLAN is created on an access switch, but its hosts cannot reach hosts in the same VLAN on a neighboring switch. The trunk is up. What is the most likely cause?
The VLAN is not allowed on the trunk or does not exist on the neighboring switch
A user's PC can ping the default gateway successfully but cannot open any websites, even by IP address. Where is the fault most likely located?
Beyond the gateway, such as upstream routing or the default route
The patch cable to the wall
An administrator raises a static route's administrative distance above the OSPF route for the same prefix. What is the intended effect?
The static route becomes a backup, used only if the OSPF route disappears
The static route is always used
A port connected to another switch keeps going into err-disabled state shortly after it comes up. BPDU guard is enabled on it. What does this indicate?
BPDU guard is mistakenly applied to a switch-to-switch link, or a loop is being detected
After a subnet was renumbered, a group of statically configured hosts lost remote connectivity while DHCP hosts recovered. What is the most likely reason?
The static hosts still use the old default gateway address
A monitoring alert fires that a DHCP scope has reached 100% utilization, and help desk tickets about 'no internet' spike. What is the connection?
New clients cannot obtain addresses because the pool is exhausted
A host was manually given an address that falls inside the active DHCP range, and now a laptop reports an address conflict. What is the best corrective action?
Exclude that address from the DHCP scope or move the host to an address outside the pool
A traceroute from a host dies at the very first hop, timing out immediately. What does this most directly point to?
A problem reaching the default gateway on the local subnet
Users report a website loads by its IP address but not by its name. Which service, not the gateway or routing, is implicated?
An inter-VLAN routing problem is suspected because VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 hosts work locally but cannot reach each other. The Layer 3 switch has SVIs for both. What is the first thing to verify?
That IP routing is enabled on the switch
A cloned virtual machine is powered on and immediately causes an address conflict with the template it came from. What is the fix?
Assign the clone a unique IP address
A router has routes to 10.0.0.0/8, 10.4.0.0/16, and 10.4.2.0/24. Which route forwards traffic to 10.4.2.75?
A department's hosts receive the wrong default gateway from DHCP after a scope edit, and none can reach other networks. What is the most efficient fix?
Correct the gateway (option 3) in the DHCP scope and renew the leases
Reconfigure each host by hand permanently
A trunk link shows a native VLAN mismatch warning in the logs. Besides the warning, what is the real risk?
Untagged traffic could leak between VLANs
A point-to-point link between two routers was configured with a /30 on one end and a /29 on the other. What symptom would this produce?
The two interfaces compute different subnets, so the link may not pass traffic correctly
A security team reports that a web server in the DMZ can be reached on HTTP but the intended rule was HTTPS only. Which configuration should be reviewed?
The ACL or firewall rule and its permitted ports
A user's laptop works perfectly at the office but has no remote access at a branch, where it was given a hard-coded office gateway. What is the best long-term fix?
Use DHCP so the laptop receives the correct gateway for each network
A routing change causes traffic to loop, and a traceroute shows the same two hops repeating. What kind of error produces this?
Misconfigured routes that point back toward each other without a valid path
After adding dozens of IoT sensors, a subnet exhausts its addresses even though the lease time is short. What is the best design fix?
Move the sensors to their own, appropriately sized subnet and scope
A host can reach its gateway and remote networks, but one specific internal server is unreachable while others respond. Which cause is LEAST likely to be the subnet mask?
If only one server is affected, the host's mask is probably fine and the server's own configuration should be checked
The host's mask is definitely wrong
A VLAN was deleted from a switch during cleanup, and every device on the affected ports lost connectivity. What is the fix?
Reassign those ports to a valid VLAN or recreate the deleted VLAN
A host is configured with a /23 mask on a network that is actually two separate /24s, and it tries to reach the neighboring /24 directly instead of through the router. What is the consequence?
Traffic to the other /24 fails because the host does not send it to the gateway
A new ACL is applied inbound on an interface, but it blocks return traffic for sessions users start. What concept was overlooked?
Stateless ACLs may need rules for established/return traffic
An administrator wants to confirm which route a router will actually use for a destination. Which command is most direct?
A device fails to get an address, the DHCP server is up and reachable, but its logs show the scope is full. Is this exhaustion or a server outage?
Exhaustion, because the server responds but has no free addresses
A redundant-gateway design uses an FHRP virtual IP, but one host was configured with a physical router IP as its gateway. What happens when that router fails?
That host loses connectivity while others using the virtual IP keep working
A switch port shows frequent topology-change notifications traced to a server that reboots often. Which configuration reduces the churn?
PortFast (edge port) on that access port
A host with a /26 mask on a network designed as /24 can only reach a quarter of its neighbors. What is the corrective action?
Change the host's mask to /24 to match the network
A duplicate IP conflict is resolved on one host, yet the conflict warnings continue. What should be investigated next?
Whether a third device or a DHCP lease is also using that address
A branch office uses a single ISP link, and the simplest way to route all non-local traffic is which option?
A static default route pointing to the ISP
Users complain that an internal application is blocked while general browsing works. The firewall team suspects a rule issue. What should they examine?
The ACL for the application's specific ports and protocols and the rule order
A host receives an address via DHCP but has no gateway listed, so it cannot leave its subnet. Which scope setting is missing?
A new 500-host subnet is addressed with a /24 and runs out of space. Which mask would have been appropriate?
A Layer 2 loop is suspected. Which command set best confirms blocked ports and instability?
show spanning-tree and show mac address-table
A host can reach everything except devices that happen to fall in the upper half of its address range, and its mask is /25 where a /24 was intended. What single change fixes it?
Which BEST summarizes how to approach common network service problems?
Isolate the layer and service involved — switching (STP, VLANs, ACLs), routing and default routes, DHCP scope, gateway, duplicate IP, or subnet mask — then verify the specific configuration
